claims.text: The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The as-solidified baseline contains minimal nano-clustering.
Annealing at approximately 0.3–0.5 T_m can induce nano-cluster formation in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The absence of Co facilitates thermally activated nano-cluster formation during controlled annealing.
Nano-cluster size, density, and stability change with temperature and strain rate.
Nano-clusters undergo formation, dissolution, and coarsening during deformation as temperature and strain rate change.
Nano-clusters act as transient obstacles to dislocation motion.
Nano-cluster formation, dissolution, or coarsening changes effective dislocation pinning.
Changes in nano-cluster-mediated dislocation pinning modulate the strength–ductility balance.
Annealed samples containing induced nano-clusters will have higher yield strength than the as-solidified baseline.
Annealed samples containing induced nano-clusters will have altered strain-rate sensitivity relative to the as-solidified baseline.
The predicted nano-cluster-related mechanical differences will be especially apparent at mid-range temperatures.
Yield strength and strain-rate sensitivity will correlate with the independently measured nano-cluster population.
The magnitude of the mechanical differences will vary systematically with annealing conditions.
The magnitude of the mechanical differences will vary systematically with dynamic-test temperature and strain rate.
The proposed mechanism operates in the temperature regime where nano-clusters can form and evolve, identified as typically 0.3–0.5 T_m.
The mechanism requires strain rates that provide sufficient time for interactions between dislocations and evolving nano-clusters.
Conditions that suppress clustering or make other dislocation-kinetic phenomena dominant fall outside the proposed mechanism's boundary.
